attempts.reason_tested: already published: canine babesiosis severity data exist
attempts.method: Case-insensitive grep for angiopoietin|Ang-2|ANGPT|Tie-2|Tie2 in /core/articles/CB*.md (444 notes) and /core/data/markdown/CB*.md. PubMed query: (dog OR dogs OR canine) AND (babesia OR babesiosis) AND (angiopoietin OR "Ang-2" OR Tie2 OR VEGF OR "vascular endothelial growth factor" OR sFlt-1 OR VEGFR), searched 2026-11-12.
attempts.result: 0 hits in CB notes and 0 in CB full texts. PubMed returned 1 record (PMID 38653059, 10.1016/j.vetpar.2024.110188 = CB122, serum extracellular-vesicle proteomics, B. canis vs healthy); it matched on a VEGF pathway enrichment term only and does not measure Ang-2. No canine babesiosis study of Ang-2 or Ang-1 exists, against severity or otherwise. Limit: PubMed only; about half the CB texts are abstract only.

attempts.reason_tested: human severity evidence weak or unverified
attempts.method: Resolved the grid DOIs in PubMed (get_article_metadata) and read the abstracts: 10.1186/s12936-016-1624-8, 10.1186/1475-2875-10-383, 10.1186/s13613-024-01393-0, 10.1186/s13054-021-03474-z; plus one extra cohort found by search, 10.1097/CCM.0000000000004469.
attempts.result: Strong. Systematic review (10.1186/s12936-016-1624-8): in all 11 falciparum studies Ang-2 rose with severity; 5 survivor/non-survivor studies AUROC 0.71-0.83. Cerebral malaria cohort, India (10.1186/1475-2875-10-383): Ang-2 AUC 0.95 for fatal CM vs mild malaria, but weak within CM. Paediatric severe malaria, Uganda, n = 464 (10.1097/CCM.0000000000004469): Ang-2 independently associated with AKI. Sepsis meta-analysis, 33 studies, 4703 patients (10.1186/s13613-024-01393-0): non-survivors SMD 1.08, AUC 0.76. Sepsis AKI, n = 228 (10.1186/s13054-021-03474-z): OR 6.07 per log. Several independent cohorts in two disease groups; grade 3 holds.

A human Ang-2 ELISA was validated for canine plasma (linearity, parallelism, precision; septic 25.5 vs healthy 6.7 ng/mL; 10.2460/ajvr.79.8.803). In canine SIRS/sepsis Ang-2 was higher in non-survivors (24.1 vs 10.2 ng/mL, AUC 0.75; 10.1111/jvim.15369). Ang-2 rose with stage in canine leishmaniosis (10.1002/vms3.70871). But the Ang-1 ELISA did NOT detect canine Ang-1 in the validation study, so the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio half of the candidate has no validated canine assay (the leishmaniosis paper reports Ang-1 with a commercial kit, unvalidated).

attempts.reason_tested: mechanism may not transfer to Babesia (cytoadherence)
attempts.method: Reasoning from the human abstracts above and the SV-06a note; no new data.
attempts.result: Weak objection. Ang-2 is released from endothelial Weibel-Palade bodies by inflammatory stimuli (TNF-alpha releases it from canine aortic endothelial cells in vitro, 10.2460/ajvr.79.8.803) and rises in bacterial sepsis and in canine SIRS without any parasite, so it does not depend on PfEMP1-type cytoadherence. Confounder to plan for: in Ugandan children Ang-2 tracked haemolysis (LDH, bilirubin) (10.1097/CCM.0000000000004469); B. rossi severity labels include haematocrit and bilirubin, so Ang-2 must be adjusted for haemolysis and anaemia, and for creatinine (AKI association). Inference, not tested.

attempts.method: grep of GN=ANGPT1|ANGPT2|TEK in /core/data/raw/DS07/B_Proteins.txt; grep of tidy files /experiments/shared/tidy/*.json; SV-06a grid columns ds06_genes and ds07_master.
attempts.result: Not in DS07 (0 matches; no master protein). Not in any tidy feature file. DS06 holds ANGPT1 and TEK RNA but not ANGPT2, in 5 experimental Beagles with no severity contrast; Ang-2 is stored protein in endothelium, so blood RNA is a poor proxy. Testable only on stored plasma: Onderstepoort CH03 citrate/EDTA samples (CB145, 97 dogs, 12 deaths) or DS07 archived serum (SRC-C, 14 complicated vs 18 uncomplicated).

verdict_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured angiopoietin-2, the human severity evidence is strong (systematic review of 11 falciparum studies, sepsis meta-analysis of 33 studies) and a validated canine Ang-2 ELISA exists with prognostic data in canine sepsis. The candidate is weakened only because Ang-1 could not be measured with the validated kit, so the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio is not assayable in dogs; the lead should be restricted to Ang-2 and adjusted for haemolysis and creatinine.

human_counterpart.claim: Ang-2 rises and Ang-1 falls with falciparum malaria severity in all 11 studies reviewed; Ang-2 separates survivors from non-survivors (AUROC 0.71-0.83)
Ang-2 and Ang-2/Ang-1 highest in fatal cerebral malaria (AUC 0.95 vs mild malaria)
Ang-2 higher in septic non-survivors (33 studies, 4703 patients, SMD 1.08)
Ang-2 associated with AKI and with haemolysis markers in paediatric severe malaria (n = 464)
Canine (non-babesial) parallel: Ang-2 higher in non-surviving dogs with SIRS or sepsis
